definition: Behavioral family therapy is a family-involved form of cognitive-behavioral therapy that helps a child or adolescent and their parents better understand the person’s condition and manage related thinking, emotion, and behavior problems. It includes family participation so parents can recognize the child’s characteristic difficulties and the support needed in everyday care.
